statement: Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system.
explanation: Venus has an average surface temperature of ~465°C. Its thick CO₂ atmosphere creates a runaway greenhouse effect that traps heat, making it hotter than Mercury despite being further from the Sun.

statement: The Sun is on fire.
explanation: The Sun is not burning in a chemical sense. It generates energy through nuclear fusion — hydrogen atoms fuse to form helium in its core, releasing enormous amounts of energy.

statement: One million Earths could fit inside the Sun.
explanation: The Sun's diameter is about 109 times that of Earth. By volume, approximately 1.3 million Earths could fit inside the Sun.

statement: Saturn is the only planet in our solar system with rings.
explanation: Jupiter, Uranus, and Neptune also have ring systems. Saturn's rings are simply far more prominent and easier to observe from Earth.

statement: Footprints left by Apollo astronauts will remain on the Moon for millions of years.
explanation: The Moon has no atmosphere, wind, or liquid water to erode them. Without these forces, the footprints could remain intact for 10 to 100 million years.

statement: There is no gravity in outer space.
explanation: Gravity extends throughout the universe. The ISS and its crew experience roughly 90% of Earth's surface gravity, but appear weightless because they are in continuous freefall.

statement: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
explanation: Venus rotates on its axis very slowly — one Venusian day lasts 243 Earth days. However, it orbits the Sun in just 225 Earth days, making its day longer than its year.

statement: The Milky Way and the Andromeda galaxy are moving away from each other.
explanation: The Milky Way and Andromeda are on a collision course. They are expected to merge in approximately 4.5 billion years to form a new elliptical galaxy.

statement: Pluto was reclassified from a planet to a dwarf planet in 2006.
explanation: The International Astronomical Union (IAU) redefined 'planet' in 2006, and Pluto did not meet the criteria of 'clearing its orbital neighbourhood', placing it in the dwarf planet category.

statement: Neutron stars are less dense than white dwarf stars.
explanation: A neutron star is one of the densest objects in the universe. A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh approximately 10 million tonnes — far denser than a white dwarf.

statement: The Great Red Spot on Jupiter is a persistent storm system.
explanation: The Great Red Spot is a high-pressure anticyclone wider than Earth. It has been continuously observed since at least the 1830s and may have existed for over 300 years.

statement: All planets in the solar system orbit the Sun in perfect circles.
explanation: As described by Kepler's First Law of Planetary Motion, all planets travel in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one focus, not at the centre of a circle.

statement: Two metal surfaces touching in a vacuum will permanently bond together.
explanation: This is known as cold welding. In space, without an oxide layer to separate them, atoms at the surfaces cannot distinguish between the two pieces of metal and bond spontaneously.

statement: Mars appears red because its surface is covered in rust.
explanation: The Martian surface is rich in iron oxide (Fe₂O₃), the same compound that gives rust its characteristic red-orange colour.

statement: Shooting stars are actual stars falling from the sky.
explanation: Shooting stars are meteors — small fragments of rock or dust that burn up due to friction as they enter Earth's atmosphere at high velocity.

statement: Uranus rotates on its side with an axial tilt of about 98 degrees.
explanation: Uranus has an axial tilt of 97.77°, meaning it essentially rolls around the Sun on its side. This is thought to be the result of a massive collision early in the solar system's history.

statement: The Moon produces its own light.
explanation: The Moon has no light source of its own. It shines by reflecting sunlight off its surface. It reflects approximately 12% of the sunlight that hits it.

statement: Astronauts grow taller in space.
explanation: Without gravity compressing the intervertebral discs, the spine decompresses. Astronauts can grow up to 5 cm (2 inches) taller during a stay on the ISS, reverting after return.

statement: Black holes act like cosmic vacuum cleaners, sucking in everything nearby.
explanation: Black holes exert gravitational attraction like any other mass. Objects at a safe orbital distance remain in orbit around them, just as planets orbit stars.

statement: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano in the solar system.
explanation: Olympus Mons stands approximately 21.9 km above the Martian datum, nearly three times the height of Mount Everest above sea level.

statement: The Sun appears yellow from Earth because it is yellow.
explanation: The Sun emits white light. It appears yellow or orange from Earth due to Rayleigh scattering, which filters shorter blue wavelengths in the atmosphere.

statement: The Apollo Guidance Computer had less processing power than a modern smartphone.
explanation: The AGC ran at 0.043 MHz with 4 KB of RAM. A modern smartphone processor is millions of times more powerful.

statement: Halley's Comet is visible from Earth approximately every 75–76 years.
explanation: Halley's Comet has an orbital period of about 75.3 years. It was last visible in 1986 and is expected to return in 2061.

statement: All stars in the night sky are in our galaxy.
explanation: The Andromeda Galaxy (M31) is visible to the naked eye from Earth as a faint smudge. It is located approximately 2.537 million light-years away.

statement: Space is completely silent.
explanation: Sound requires a medium to travel through. Interstellar space is an extremely high vacuum, meaning there are not enough molecules to propagate sound waves.
